page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix multiplication. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier performance in database operations and image processing. It registers strong results in multi-core Geekbench testing, software compilation, ray tracing, and Passmark CPU tests, including physics and encryption. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is strong at 4457.66 GB/sec, though uncached large block read and write speeds fall into the average range. The server also demonstrates strong throughput for static web serving and Redis SET operations.

This server is suited for compute-intensive workloads that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. The presence of Intel AMX instructions supports CPU-based machine learning tasks, as evidenced by strong prompt processing and text generation speeds for small and medium LLM models. However, text generation for large 70B models drops to average speeds. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly efficient for CPU-bound tasks like software compilation, cryptography, and database operations, while memory-bound applications requiring massive datasets per core may face limitations due to the 2.0 GB per core memory allocation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized x86_64 server featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical Intel cores and 128 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance relies on its high-density CPU configuration and a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmark results place the server in the top tier for database operations and image processing, with strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and multi-core processing. It also exhibits strong throughput for Redis SET operations and static web serving. The 2.0 GB of RAM per core makes it highly efficient for compute-bound tasks, though it is less suited for memory-heavy applications. This server is recommended for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, cryptography, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
